---
title: "What a solver must provide"
---

This repository runs nothing. To use a case here you bring your own solver.
This page lists what that solver has to be able to do, so the gap can be
measured before the work starts.

## For the two published benchmarks

**An incompressible, five-layer, self-gravitating spherical earth** with a
Maxwell viscoelastic mantle, a purely elastic lithosphere and an inviscid
fluid core, using the core-mantle boundary conditions of Wu and Ni (1996).
That is [M3-L70-V01](earth-models.qmd#m3-l70-v01). A compressible solver has
to be able to approximate it, or the comparison measures compressibility and
not the code.

**Loading Love numbers to degree 256**, elastic and fluid, with their
relaxation spectrum, for the wavenumber-domain tests. Tidal Love numbers for
test 3/1. Degree one in the centre of mass frame for test 7/1.

**Surface fields for an analytic axisymmetric load**: vertical and horizontal
displacement and geoid height, on a colatitude grid, at prescribed epochs.

**The sea level equation** at three levels for the Martinec cases: not solved
for case A, solved on a fixed ocean geometry for cases B and C, and solved on
a time-varying geometry with floating ice for cases D and E.

## For GIAMIP

**The prescribed grid**, 257 latitudes by 513 longitudes, Gauss-Legendre. A
solver on a different internal grid must interpolate while conserving ice
mass, which the protocol asks for explicitly in section 2.2.1.

**Ten output variables**, four gridded and six scalar time series. The six
scalars are mass and area integrals, and protocol section 6.1 requires them
to be computed on the solver's own grid before any interpolation, so they
cannot be recovered from the gridded output afterwards. They are:

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
import json, pathlib
v = json.loads((pathlib.Path("../..") / "giamip" / "resources"
                / "variables.json").read_text())
rows = ["| Variable | Dimensions | Unit | Precision | Long name |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"]
for e in v["variables"]:
    if not e["mandatory"]:
        continue
    rows.append(f"| `{e['variable']}` | {e['dim']} | `{e['units']}` | "
                f"{e['precision']} | {e['long_name']} |")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

**PREM-stable as the elastic structure, compressible, with continuous
density.** Protocol v4.0 Section 3.1 gives PREM-stable as the PREM of every
experiment that names PREM, and asks each group to state in the model report
(question Q14) which PREM file it used, whether its earth is compressible, and
how it discretises density. The G-ADOPT answers are the same in every
experiment: the file `giamip/PREM-stable.csv`, version v1.0.0 of
doi:10.5281/zenodo.23178246; a compressible earth, with the bulk modulus of the
file; and a continuous density, linear between the nodes of the file.
`giamip.earth` gives these values at any radius (see
[the Python interface](python-interface.qmd)). A solver with constant-density
layers takes the volume average of PREM-stable in each layer and states its
layer boundaries.

**The centre of mass frame of the whole Earth system**, with the treatment of
degree one documented.

**Output in the prescribed form**: one NetCDF file per variable, named
`[variable]_[experiment]_[member]_[group]_[model].nc`, dimensions ordered
`(time, lat, lon)`, latitude south to north, longitude in `[0, 360)`, no fill
value attribute, and four global attributes naming the group, the model and
the contributors. The compliance checker rejects a file whose experiment,
member, group or model name contains an underscore.

## Where the two solvers stand

Recorded so the gap is visible. Neither is work for this repository.

### lovejx

A one-dimensional Love number and sea level code in Python and JAX,
at [g-adopt/lovejx](https://github.com/g-adopt/lovejx). It was called sl1d, and then radopt, before September 2026.

| Requirement | State |
| --- | --- |
| M3-L70-V01 | Missing. lovejx ships PREM variants only, so the deck has to be written. |
| Incompressible earth | The kernel has an incompressible matrix, so this is a deck and a code path, not new physics. |
| 513 longitudes | Missing. `GaussLegendreGrid.build` raises `ValueError("nlon must be even")`. |
| The six scalar integrals | Missing. `SeaLevelResult` returns displacement, geoid and relative sea level. It holds the grounded ice mask internally and returns neither it nor any integral. |
| Centre of mass frame | Not exposed. |
| Sea level equation | Present, with rotational feedback. |

### G-ADOPT

A three-dimensional finite element geodynamics framework built on Firedrake.
It already carries a Spada benchmark case in `tests/3d_spada`. The GIAMIP
requirements have not been assessed against it.
